summary: Fix orphan referrer_id values by setting them to NULL, then add the ForeignKey constraint, deploy the new version with state_only migration, and retire the old version, ensuring both versions remain consistent during overlap.
write_consistency: The referrer_id column remains nullable integer; orphan rows are nulled before the FK is added, so the old version (which does not write to referrer_id during save) and the new version (which enforces the FK) can coexist without constraint violations.
revision_notes: Previous plan failed because adding the FK constraint directly on account_user.referrer_id violated existing rows with referrer_id values not present in account_user.id (orphan references). Root cause: pre-existing data contained invalid FK references. Revised plan first nullifies orphan referrer_id rows, then adds the constraint, preserving compatibility with the old pinned version that ignores the column during save().

stages.description: Set orphan referrer_id values to NULL so the subsequent FK constraint can be added without violation.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);

stages.description: Add ForeignKey constraint on referrer_id referencing account_user id.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id);

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version after the new version is live and the FK constraint is confirmed.
